Thanks a lot for your attention and support!

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Seasonal package requires binary executable files. How to deal with that?
parts:
Danilo,

The approach should be possible. Though I am not aware of anyone who has done this before.

Another question: Do you require a specific version of the X-13ARIMA data? Would it make sense for ShinyApps to automatically install the latest version from the US Census website when it detects you're using the seasonal package? We do something similar for other packages that have 3rd party dependencies.

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Seasonal package requires binary executable files. How to deal with that?
parts:
Hello!

I've tried to solve my problem by pasting the linux binary files in a new folder named 'linux'. Then I ask R for the running operating system and according to the answer I provide to seasonal package the appropriate file path. Here follows my code:

var_os <- switch(Sys.info()[['sysname']], Windows= 1, Linux  = 2)
path_windows <- file.path(getwd(),"X13/x13ashtml")
path_linux <- file.path(getwd(),"X13/linux/x13ashtml")
if(var_os==1){ Sys.setenv(X13_PATH = path_windows ) }
if(var_os==2){ Sys.setenv(X13_PATH = path_linux ) }


It works perfectly when I run it from my PC, however it doesn't work properly when I use deployApp() to upload it to shinyapps.io . As I am a new user, I would like to know if it is possible to either check the folders where my code is hosted in shinyapp.io or get the error message from the linux server.

Danilo
